title: Claims Advocate (Path to Licensed Public Adjuster)
blurb: Salaried NY seat that pays for your public adjuster license while you learn financial-loss claim advocacy.
description: United Public Adjusters & Appraisers is hiring a Claims Advocate at its Melville, Long Island office, aimed at people coming from accounting, finance, insurance customer service, or claims.

The firm covers licensing and training so the hire can become a licensed public adjuster within a few months, then work business interruption, builder's risk, and property damage files using financial records to support the claim.
The page lists a $75k–$85k salary (based on experience) plus bonus, health benefits, and PTO; submit a resume through the careers page.

title: Property Insurance Claims Adjuster
blurb: Experienced property adjuster to run policyholder claims from intake to settlement for a Long Island PA firm.
description: United Public Adjusters & Appraisers wants a seasoned property adjuster, from either the carrier or public side, to manage residential and commercial claims for policyholders.

The work is mostly in the office: reviewing estimates, engineering reports, and policy language, building claim packages, and negotiating with carriers, with some joint inspections in the field. It asks for 3+ years of property adjusting and a NY public adjuster license or willingness to get one.
Pay is listed at $75k–$110k plus medical coverage and PTO.

title: Insurance Claims Manager
blurb: Leadership role steering a portfolio of policyholder property claims and mentoring the adjuster team.
description: United Public Adjusters & Appraisers is hiring a Claims Manager to coordinate strategy and day-to-day progress on residential and commercial property claims for policyholders.

The manager oversees active files, mentors adjusters and support staff, negotiates settlements, and makes sure files are ready for appraisal, mediation, or litigation. Requirements include 5+ years in property claims and Xactimate experience; a NYS public adjuster license is preferred.
The posting lists a $110k–$130k salary with medical coverage and PTO.

title: Public Adjuster
blurb: Licensed Texas PA to inspect, estimate, and negotiate claims while helping grow a Houston franchise office.
description: Tiger Adjusters, a franchise-based public adjusting firm, is looking for an experienced licensed public adjuster for its Houston market.

Full-time, with pay negotiated based on experience; the posting asks applicants to email a resume and LinkedIn profile.

Full-time, with pay negotiated based on experience; applicants send a resume per the posting.

Compensation starts as a $50k–$65k draw against uncapped commission, with health, dental, vision, and 401(k) benefits.

Pay depends on experience, and healthcare and a 401(k) are offered.

Applicants need a Florida 3-20 public adjuster license or a 31-20 apprentice license, with bond in good standing. The work includes networking with roofers, plumbers, contractors, and property managers for leads, keeping clients updated, and meeting carrier adjusters at inspections.
Xactimate, negotiation skills, and being bilingual are all pluses.

The role builds referral relationships with chambers of commerce, networking groups, contractors, real estate agents, and local businesses, sets up in-person and virtual meetings, and helps home and business owners understand their coverage.

description: Velocity Public Adjusting (VPA) is hiring Loss Documentation Field Inspectors who travel across the U.S. about 75% of the time to inspect and document property damage for its policyholder clients. No relocation is required.

Inspectors go top to bottom on each property, including roofs, interiors, and structure, and capture detailed photos and written reports from a coverage point of view rather than a contractor's, working with insureds, engineers, and VPA's internal team.

The job is salaried with full benefits and no commission. VPA looks for field adjusting, inspection, or loss documentation experience and says it suits independent adjusters and newer public adjusters. Apply on the posting page.

The adjuster handles property claims start to finish: inspecting losses, building estimates and documentation, advising clients, negotiating settlements, and signing both new and in-house leads. It asks for a valid Pennsylvania and/or New Jersey PA license, two or more years of relevant experience, and damage estimating skills (Xactimate a plus).
Pay is salary plus commission based on experience, with healthcare and a 401(k). Apply through the posting or by emailing a resume to the firm.

location: New York Tri-State Area (field, vehicle required)

The estimator writes detailed repair estimates in Xactimate, flags code upgrades and hidden damage carrier adjusters often miss, and supports public adjusters, contents specialists, and claim managers with documentation and joint inspections.
Requirements include at least 3 years of property damage estimating or construction experience, Xactimate proficiency, and a reliable vehicle. Submit a resume through the careers page.

description: United Public Adjusters & Appraisers wants a contents adjuster at its Melville, Long Island office to document and value personal property lost or damaged in fires, water losses, storms, and other insured events.

The adjuster builds detailed inventories, researches replacement values, works with field adjusters and estimators, and prepares contents reports for carriers. Prior contents claims experience and familiarity with pricing tools are expected.
The posting lists a $70k–$90k salary plus health benefits. Submit a resume through the careers page.

The role works existing relationships with property owners, managers, resident managers, and supers, represents the firm at industry events, manages a pipeline in the CRM, and helps on site visits. Hires must get a public adjuster license within 90 days, with training provided.
Pay is salary plus commission with fully paid benefits; a proven sales record and Manhattan real estate connections are expected. Submit a resume through the careers page.

Pay starts with a $50k–$65k draw against uncapped commission after a 30–60 day probation, plus health, dental, vision, and a 401(k). A public adjuster license is required within a month of hire, and a business degree or five years of sales experience is expected. Apply through the posting.
